text: "Look toward heaven, and count the stars." The Hebrew word also means to tell the story. God was showing Abraham the gospel.
explanation:
It always seemed strange that Abraham was counted righteous just for looking at stars he couldn't number. But the word is saphar, the root of sepher, a book: to recount, to tell. And Psalm 19 says the same: "The heavens declare the glory of God… Day unto day utters speech, and night unto night reveals knowledge. There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard."

Before there was a Bible, God wrote the story of the coming Seed across the night sky, the same sky seen from Singapore, New York and Timbuktu. Abraham looked up, heard the story of the One who would come from him, and believed. "And He accounted it to him for righteousness." You believe the same gospel, written now in a Book.

text: He counts the stars and calls them all by name, and He heals the brokenhearted.
explanation:
With all our telescopes, no one has ever counted the stars. Yet "He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by name." And look at the verse just before it: "He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds."

The God who runs the universe isn't too busy for your heart. At every party, however glittering, there are broken hearts, and He sees each one. Jesus said He was anointed "to heal the brokenhearted." Bring Him yours tonight.

text: "Your seed and her Seed." Women don't carry the seed. The Bible's very first prophecy announced a virgin birth.
explanation:
Right after the fall, God spoke to the serpent: "I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her Seed; He shall crush your head, and you shall crush His heel." The seed belongs to the man, so the Seed of the woman pointed to a Son born without a human father.

Notice too that the Champion would be wounded in the fight: a crushed heel for a crushed head. Which would you rather have? At the cross, Jesus was struck, but Satan's head was broken. "When the fullness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman."

text: The story in the stars begins with Virgo, the virgin holding the seed, and ends with Leo, the lion. So does the gospel.
explanation:
Strip away later astrology and look at the old star pictures. Virgo holds a branch and an ear of grain; her brightest star, Spica, means the seed, and the Hebrew name speaks of the Branch, a title of the Messiah. Next comes Libra, the scales of justice, with a slain lamb and the Southern Cross beneath it: what balanced the scales was the Lamb on the cross.

The last sign is Leo, whose brightest star sits at the lion's foot, the foot that crushes. The New Testament opens with a virgin and a promised Child, and closes with "Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah… has prevailed." Don't look to the stars to guide your life. Look to the One who made them and wrote His story in them.

text: The priest examined the lamb, not the sinner. Today God looks at Jesus to assess you.
explanation:
When someone brought a lamb to the altar, it was obvious why he was there: he had sinned. So the priest didn't inspect the man; he inspected the lamb for blemishes. The man laid his hands on it, his sin passed to the innocent animal, and its innocence counted for him.

When the enemy points at your thoughts, your feelings, your envy, your failures, point him to your Lamb. "Behold! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!" The question isn't how good you are. It's how perfect He is, and He is without spot.

text: God hates sin the way you'd hate a cancer in your child: because He loves the person so much.
explanation:
You don't think much about a tumour in a stranger. But if it's in someone you love, you hate it fiercely, as much as you love them. That's why God hates sin. Sin spreads like a cancer, and it destroys the people He loves.

Yet He never confuses the person with the disease. Jesus judged leprosy and healed the leper; He cast out the demon and loved the man. "The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." He removed the cancer by bearing it Himself, so He could keep you.

text: Righteousness is a gift. How do you receive a gift? You say, "Thank you."
explanation:
When a father hands his son a new toy, the boy doesn't earn it or negotiate for it. He says "Thank you," and it's his. That's how righteousness works now. Not by keeping the Ten Commandments (even David failed), but by believing on Jesus, the way Abraham believed.

And once you're righteous, every promise to the righteous is yours: "Blessings are on the head of the righteous." "The seed of the righteous shall be delivered." "No grave trouble will overtake the righteous." Thank Him for the gift, and expect His blessings.
